---
title: "Model fixes and the GP / embedding comparison"
subtitle: "Five fixes found while comparing the paper's embedding systems, and what the comparison shows"
date: 2026-09-29
---

# Summary

* Five defects were found and fixed while setting up the comparison. Fixes 1, 2, 4 and 5 were also
  present in the code the paper's hardware flights used (tag `archive/main-2026-05-02`), and in the code
  of the paper's SITL runs.
* **The GP decides whether the certificate is true when the wind drifts; the embedding system barely
  matters here.** In the numerical runs (the paper's evolving wind) the time-varying GP keeps the vehicle
  inside its certified tube with every embedding system (0 % of the time outside); a time-invariant GP is
  violated about 40 % of the time, by up to 0.29 m. The SITL world has no wind, so SITL cannot show this.
* With the time-varying GP the three embedding systems certify the same horizon with the same tubes;
  (66)-(67) is the cheapest (about a third less compute per rollout).
* In SITL a **5 cm model-mismatch margin** on $\delta$ (now the default) takes the time the vehicle spends
  outside its certified tube from 19 % to 0 % (all six variants: 0-0.02 %), at the price of a shorter
  certified horizon (0.34 s).

# The five fixes

| | what was wrong | effect | fix |
|-|--------|--------|--------|
| 1 | the embedding used $+[M_u]K$, but the controller applies $u = u_r - K(x - x_r)$ | the tube modelled the wrong closed loop (looser than needed) | $K_p = -K$ in (66)-(69); certifies 0.45-0.62 s instead of 0.40-0.53 s on the same plans |
| 2 | the dynamics' Jacobian was taken over $w \in \mu(x_r) \pm s$ only | the $\partial/\partial\theta$ entries depend on $w$; the domain must contain every disturbance the box can produce | domain $[\underline\gamma, \overline\gamma]$ over the box, for all variants |
| 3 | `RolloutPlan.index_at` truncated exact row times ($0.03/0.01 = 2.999\ldots \to 2$) | 45 % of numerical ticks used the previous row (controller and metrics) | $+10^{-6}$ row tolerance (Python and C++) |
| 4 | the planar state's $h, v$ were filled with **inertial** $(v_y, v_z)$; the model defines them in the **body** frame | up to 1.7 m/s off at 30° roll, in the tube's start state and the RTA feedback | $[h; v] = R(\theta)^\top [v_y; v_z]$ (Python and C++) |
| 5 | the state came from the `mocap_px4_relays` relay: a 25 ms timer behind a 50 Hz rate gate that local position (exactly 50 Hz) keeps failing | 25 Hz with gaps up to 150 ms, i.e. stale state | the node and the C++ loop read `/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry` (100 Hz) directly |

Effect of fixes 4 and 5 on a default SITL flight:

| | before | + body-frame $h, v$ | + 100 Hz PX4 odometry |
|----------|-----|-----|-----|
| tracking RMSE lateral / vertical | 88 / 67 mm | 28 / 43 mm | **20 / 32 mm** |
| worst position outside the certified tube | 0.45 m | 0.21 m | **0.11 m** |
| C++ fast loop, RMSE lateral / vertical | 86 / 50 mm | | **23 / 28 mm** |

**New metric: escapes.** `analysis.tube_escapes` measures, at every certified control tick, how far the
vehicle's position is outside the certified box of the row in use: the true state in the numerical
simulation, the EKF2 estimate in SITL and on hardware. A certificate that is correct has no escapes
beyond the 10 ms integration step of the tube (about 1 mm).

**The remaining SITL gap, and the model-mismatch margin.** With $\delta = 0$ the TV-GPR flights
still leave the tube about 20 % of the time (up to 0.12 m). The escapes happen in the **first 0.1 s of
each plan** (40-46 % of those ticks, about 1 % once a plan is older than 0.4 s), while the tube, which
starts from the estimated state with a ±0.5 mm box, is millimetres wide: in its first moments the real
vehicle departs from the planar model's prediction (rate-loop lag, out-of-plane motion; drag is weak,
$-0.08$ N per m/s). The threshold does not reach this part of the tube: at 0.5 m instead of 0.25 m the
time outside is 16 % (worst 0.13 m). A **model-mismatch margin** on $\delta$ does, and is now the default
(`--model-mismatch-margin 0.05`: $\delta = \max(0.05\,\text{m}, \text{estimate uncertainty})$):

| TV-GPR + (68)-(69), PX4 SITL, 3 flights each | $\delta = 0$ | **$\delta = 0.05$ m** | $\delta = 0.1$ m |
|----------------|------|------|------|
| time outside the certified tube / worst | 19 % / 0.12 m | **0 % / 1 mm** | 0 % / 0 |
| outside in a plan's first 0.1 s | 46 % | 0 % | 0 % |
| certified horizon, median / 5th percentile | 0.54 / 0.42 s | 0.35 / 0.28 s | 0.25 / 0.21 s |
| plans in 20 s | 41 | 83 | 98 |
| tracking RMSE lateral / vertical | 20 / 27 mm | 13 / 16 mm | 10 / 11 mm |

The price is a shorter horizon and twice the replanning (a rollout takes about 5 ms, so the margin to
the 0.35 s horizon stays large); tracking improves partly because the reference is re-anchored at the
vehicle twice as often. The numerical simulation keeps $\delta = 0$: its model is the vehicle.

# The comparison

Two wind models (TV-GPR, $\epsilon = 0.25$; GPR = TVGPR with $\epsilon = 0$) × the paper's three
embedding systems (Appendix A), all at the same certificate: position within 0.25 m of the reference,
0.3 m floor. **Numerical** closed loop: the paper's evolving wind, which **drifts over time**; exact model;
10 cases per variant (calm, ×0.3 / ×0.6 / ×1.0 with 3 seeds), backup off, $\delta = 0$. **PX4 SITL**: 3
flights per variant, backup on, flown with $\delta = 0$ and with the default 5 cm margin. The Gazebo world
has **no wind** (`default.sdf`; `windy.sdf` only blows a constant 5 × 2 m/s), so in SITL the GPs learn a
steady thrust offset: SITL tests the model mismatch, not the wind model.

Numerical, drifting wind (9 wind runs per variant): time outside the certified tube, worst excursion:

| embedding system | **TV-GPR** | GPR |
|---|---|---|
| (68)-(69): first order in $u$ and $w$ | **A: 0 %, 0.9 mm** (default) | D: 41 %, 0.10 m |
| (66)-(67): first order in $u$ | **E: 0 %, 0.9 mm** | C: 40 %, 0.29 m |
| (64)-(65): no first-order terms | **F: 0.03 %, 1.2 mm** | B: 40 %, 0.28 m |

| | A | E | F | D | C | B |
|---------------|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| numerical: certified horizon (median) | 0.59 s | 0.59 s | 0.59 s | 0.78 s | 0.80 s | 0.70 s |
| numerical: tube half-width at +0.25 s | 26 mm | 26 mm | 25 mm | 2.6 mm | 2.5 mm | 2.4 mm |
| numerical: rollout | 6.9 ms | 4.3 ms | 6.8 ms | 7.0 ms | 6.1 ms | 6.2 ms |
| SITL, $\delta = 0$: time outside the tube | 19 % | 20 % | 20 % | 65 % | 67 % | 71 % |
| SITL, $\delta = 0$: worst excursion | 0.12 m | 0.12 m | 0.15 m | 0.27 m | 0.80 m | 0.26 m |
| **SITL, 5 cm margin: time outside the tube** | **0 %** | **0 %** | **0 %** | **0 %** | **0 %** | **0.02 %** |
| SITL, 5 cm margin: certified horizon | 0.34 s | 0.34 s | 0.34 s | 0.17 s | 0.29 s | 0.29 s |
| SITL, 5 cm margin: tracking lateral / vertical (mm) | 13 / 18 | 13 / 16 | 12 / 15 | 7 / 9 | 11 / 12 | 12 / 11 |

**Why the GP matters (numerical).** The time-invariant GP's uncertainty stays small near its 9
observations, so its tubes are about 10× thinner and certify further ahead; but the wind drifts over
time, so the GP is confidently wrong and the vehicle leaves the "certified" tube about 40 % of the time,
by up to 0.29 m. The TV-GPR's forgetting grows the uncertainty over the look-ahead, which keeps the tube
honest: no escapes with any embedding system.

**Why the embedding barely matters.** With TV-GPR the growth of $\sigma$ along the look-ahead dominates
the tube's growth, so the first-order disturbance term of (68)-(69) buys no measurable tightening over
(66)-(67); and for this vehicle (64)-(65) coincides with (66)-(67), because the inputs enter through a
constant selector matrix: $[M_u](K[e]) = ([M_u]K)[e]$. A benefit of the first-order terms would need a
disturbance whose mean varies across the tube much more than its uncertainty grows along it.

**What SITL shows.** With $\delta = 0$ every variant leaves its tube in the first moments of each plan,
the thinner GPR tubes more often (65-71 % against 19-20 %); this is the planar model's mismatch with the
PX4 vehicle, not a wind-model failure (there is no drifting wind). With the 5 cm margin all six variants
stay inside their tubes and none needed the LAND backup; the TV-GPR variants certify the longest, while
the GPR variants replan up to 1.6× as often, which re-anchors the reference and lowers their tracking
error. The failure of the time-invariant GP can only be reproduced in SITL with a time-varying wind in
Gazebo.

Data, tables (GP × embedding grids, two-way effect split, both SITL sets), per-flight results and figures:
`packages/px4_rta_mm_gpr/scripts/data_analysis/05_embedding_comparison.ipynb`. Reproduce with
`--gp tv|static --embedding uw|u|none --model-mismatch-margin 0.05` (node) or
`SimConfig(gp_epsilon=..., embedding=...)`.
